body: Then this sounds like a bug. We will investigate and get back to you.
@junit-team/junit-lambda I think `JUnit5TestableFactory` should not throw exceptions when it cannot resolve selectors because other TestEngines might. What do you think?

I think you're right. An unresolvable selector should just be ignored. An
unresolvable unique ID however should lead to an exception.

Trying to discover methods and classes that are not JUnit5 tests or containers are now being logged and ignored as in JUnit4.

I'm not sure we should do the same with:
- Unique IDs that do not follow the correct unique ID syntax
- Classes or methods from Unique IDs that do not exist

IMO, at least the first one should throw an exception since it means that the IDE (or any other client for that matter) is doing something wrong.

To the first one: I have problems with JUnit4TestCaseWithRunnerWithCustomUniqueIds. No tests are run and the warning is shown. Not sure that I understand how should IDE detect that it is special, especially when all tests from package are run
I have support for junit 5 locally, so I run the test without @RunWith(JUnit5.class). Unfortunately I can't share the details now, will post the trace tomorrow.
